page.layout: Two woodcut coin medallions at the top of the page, side by side, with no text of their own; below them one column of running text in two paragraphs. No marginal notes. Running head centred at top; page number at top left.

main_text.l: CLAVDIVS, Drufi Germanici ex minore Antonia fi-
lius, Liuillæ & alterius Drufi frater, Romæ post Caligulam im-
perat anno mundi 4004. à Christo nato 42. Hic Lugduni
natus est, quem mater portentum hominis dictitabat: auia Au-
gusta pro despectis. semper habuit: soror Liuilla, cum audisset
imperaturum, tam iniquam fortem pop. Ro. palam detestata
est. Fortunæ ludibrio ad imperium, cum latitaret extrema per-
timescens, interfecto Caligula, venit: quod non minore socor-
dia quàm crudelitate per annos ferè 14. vexauit. Britanniæ
bellum intulit, eámque in deditionem accepit. Orcades insu-
las Ro. imperio addidit. Hic Messalina uxore sua uixdum sup-
plicio affecta, quòd C. Silio nupsisset, Agrippinam Germanici
fratris filiam, nouo exemplo, liberis duobus nouercam super-
induxit: cùm paulò ante pro concione confirmasset, quatenus
sibi male cederent matrimonia, in cœlibatu se permansurum,
ac nisi permansisset, non recusaturum confodi manibus ipso-
rum. Præterea Britannico filio priuignum Neronem antepo-
fuit: cuius insidiis, & Agrippinæ matris, veneno in boleto dato
periit, anno ætatis 64. imperij 4. exortus crinitæ stellæ, ta-
ctúmque de cœlo monumentum Drufi patris, præsagia mortis
eius præcipua fuere: & in ultima cognitione pro tribunali ac-
cessisse se ad vitæ terminum semel atque iterum pronuntia-
uit. Vide Sueto.in Claud.Cæs.
AEMILIA Lepida, Augusti proneptis, Pauli AEmilij
Censoris filij, & Iuliæ, neptis Augusti, filia, prima omnium
desponsata est Claudio: sed eam, quòd parentes eius Augu-
stum offenderant, virginem adhuc repudiauit. Sueto.in Clau.

page.notes: Coin legends are part of the woodcut illustrations, not printed text. Left medallion: a laureate head of Claudius, legend reading roughly "TI CLAVDIVS CAES AVG P M TR P IMP P P". Right medallion: a draped female bust of Aemilia Lepida, legend reading roughly "AEMILIA LEPID CL IMP VXOR AVG". Long s is set as an s-like form throughout; transcribed as plain s. Numerals are old-style figures, copied as printed. The printed "tactúmque" carries an acute accent, kept as printed.
